newsitem.title: GERMANY: HOCKEY-ANNAN SCORES GOLDEN GOAL FOR AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: HOCKEY-ANNAN SCORES GOLDEN GOAL FOR AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Alyson Annan scored hockey's first "golden goal" in a major event to give Olympic champions Australia a 2-1 win over Germany in the final of the women's Champions' Trophy tournament on Sunday.

Germany held the Australians to a 1-1 draw in 70 minutes for the second time in the tournament but the Olympic champions made sure of their fourth successive title when Annan scored in the 78th minute, 10 seconds before the end of the first of two periods of sudden death extra time.
Annan rounded goalkeeper Julia Zwehl to score after both countries had had a good chance in extra time.
Annan had an outstanding tournament, finishing as top scorer and being voted player of the tournament.
The golden goal rule was introduced by the International Hockey Federation after the Atlanta Olympics.
By winning on Sunday Australia retained all three of the world's major women's titles -- Olympic Games, World Cup and Champions' Trophy.

Germany, very much the underdogs, made the perfect start when Britta Becker gave them the lead in the third minute. She volleyed the ball down into the backboard when the Australian goalkeeper padded a shot into the air.
Australia levelled within five minutes, Katrina Powell hitting home a fine shot from the circle's edge following a German defensive error.
Earlier, the Netherlands avenged a defeat by South Korea in the round robin games when they beat the Olympic silver medallists 5-2 in the third place playoff. Suzan van der Wielen scored a hat-trick.
